Task — commit my F2 fix locally on a branch, then run the four-axis
cross-platform audit against it. Verifier mode throughout: you execute
mechanics and audit; you NEVER author or modify fix/test content.

HARD GATE — Phase 0 runs first and gates everything: this protocol assumes
I have ALREADY written the fix and regression test as uncommitted changes
in the working tree. If the tree contains no such changes, STOP and report
"fix not yet authored" — do NOT write any fix or test yourself, under any
framing. That work is mine.

Allowed mutations: creating branch f2-harvest-fix + exactly ONE commit on
it; rebasing that branch onto master (abort on any conflict); fast-forward
of local master to upstream/master; restaging pre-commit auto-fixes (report
each verbatim); /tmp/xplat-test/**; uv python install (uv-managed only);
git worktree add/remove under /tmp/xplat-test/ + prune; report files under
scratch/hunt/. Forbidden: git push; any content edit to fix or test beyond
pre-commit auto-fixes; touching .venv (--no-sync on any in-repo uv run);
shell profiles.

PHASE 0 — Gate + diff audit
- git status --porcelain → expected: tracked modifications implementing the
  fix (untracked diff_test.py is known and fine). Tree clean → HARD GATE
  STOP. Any tracked change outside (a) the deconstruct_function harvest in
  tinygrad/uop/ops.py and (b) one test file → STOP, list the strays.
- git diff → record pass/fail per item, quoting lines on any fail:
  harvest-loop change only (~ops.py:1331-1338); closure assert untouched;
  TEST_PICKLE return line untouched; test calls deconstruct_function
  directly; victim global referenced ONLY inside a genexpr-inside-a-lambda
  (a listcomp victim is vacuous on 3.12+ via PEP 709 — if I used a
  listcomp, flag it as a MUST-FIX finding); membership-style assertions;
  no Tensor/device/engine imports; no env flags set. Failures here are
  Axis-3 findings — record and continue; only strays stop the commit.

PHASE 1 — Branch + commit
- git checkout -b f2-harvest-fix
- pre-commit run --files <each changed file>; if hooks auto-fix, restage
  and report exactly what they changed.
- git commit with EXACTLY this message:
  "<EDIT BEFORE PASTING — e.g.: fix deconstruct_function to harvest
  globals from nested code objects>"
- Record the commit sha.

PHASE 2 — Sync + rebase
- git fetch upstream; record upstream/master sha (was 83971860d at last
  check; take whatever is current).
- git checkout master && git merge --ff-only upstream/master (tree is
  clean now, so this is safe) && git checkout f2-harvest-fix
- git rebase master. On ANY conflict: git rebase --abort, flag prominently,
  and continue the audit from the pre-rebase base.
- Record final branch sha and BASE = $(git merge-base master f2-harvest-fix).

PHASE 3 — Four-axis audit
Worktrees: /tmp/xplat-test/pre at BASE, /tmp/xplat-test/post at
f2-harvest-fix. Sanity: git diff BASE..f2-harvest-fix --stat = fix + test
files only.

AXIS 4 — the matrix we're judged by: parse .github/workflows/*.yml; table
of (job, runs-on, python-version, env flags, test commands) →
scratch/hunt/ci_matrix.md. Mark the process-replay job RESIDUAL (only
meaningful in the real PR context). VERSIONS = CI's Pythons ∪ {3.11, 3.12,
3.13, 3.14} ∩ requires-python; uv python install any missing; record.

AXIS 3 — backend axis killed by construction: the Phase-0 checklist
results, restated as the formal pass/fail list.

AXIS 1 — Python-version grid. For each V in VERSIONS × {pre, post}, via
`uv run --no-project --python V --with-editable <worktree> --with pytest`:
  1. Regression test → must FAIL on pre for the intended reason (the
     missed-global miss, not an import/collection error — verify the
     failure text) and PASS on post, on EVERY V.
  2. Harvest-delta audit: use my existing callback walker from scratch/hunt/
     if present (adapt invocation); else write a dump script in
     /tmp/xplat-test/ that walks all registered PatternMatcher callbacks
     and emits {callback: sorted ha…[truncated for dataset]
Verifier mode. **Phase 0 — the hard gate** — checking whether your fix exists as uncommitted tracked changes:

# Gate report

**Stopped at Phase 0: fix not yet authored.** The protocol's premise — your fix and regression test sitting as uncommitted tracked changes — isn't true of this tree. Checked three ways: porcelain (only the known untracked `diff_test.py`), empty `git diff --stat` (nothing modified or staged), and no fix branch or stash anywhere local. The skip clause for a clean-tree-plus-existing-branch leg doesn't apply since no branch exists. Nothing was created, committed, or audited; [xplat_report_M1.md](scratch/hunt/xplat_report_M1.md) now carries a dated addendum so whichever leg runs next sees current state.

To make the gate pass on the next run, this checkout needs your uncommitted edits to exactly two places: the `deconstruct_function` harvest (tinygrad/uop/ops.py:1331-1338) and one test file. The authoring constraints the Phase-0 diff audit will enforce are listed in the stop-report — the load-bearing one remains the **genexpr-inside-a-lambda** victim, since a listcomp victim goes vacuous on 3.12+ via PEP 709.

One protocol defect to fix before re-running, separate from the gate: the Phase-1 commit message is still the literal unedited placeholder (`"<EDIT BEFORE PASTING — e.g.: …>"`). The instruction says commit with EXACTLY that message — had the gate passed, your single allowed commit would have carried a template string. Worth editing now so the next run doesn't trip on it.

Stopping here per the hard gate.
